summary: Ephemeral SSO token exchange drops delegated_support role; users blocked from Oncall Snapshot tool
description: Issue summary: When users sign into the Oncall Snapshot internal tool via ephemeral SSO (browser-based short-lived token flow), the delegated_support role is missing from the final access token after the token-exchange step. Impact: multiple engineers cannot open runbooks or capture oncall snapshots; affects scheduled incident response and paging. Environment: production (us-west), affects users authenticating via Okta ephemeral session (device-trust enabled) and using the SSO->TokenExchange flow implemented by sso-proxy/token-service. User-visible symptom: 403 Forbidden with RBAC deny for delegated_support-scoped endpoints.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to console.redwood.internal with Okta SSO (device-trust). 2) From the console, click 'Open Oncall Snapshot'. 3) sso-proxy initiates token-exchange with token-service to mint ephemeral application token. 4) Final request to /api/snapshots returns 403. Observed claim set on returned token does not include 'roles: ["delegated_support"]' despite Okta session containing delegated_support group claim.

comments: 2026-03-13T16:05:10Z - Liam O'Connor: Acknowledged; I've reproduced locally using a dev Okta session. Token-service returns roles array with only console_user. Investigating claim-mapping rules in sso-proxy.

2026-03-13T17:10:44Z - Nikhil Rao (Auth Eng): We rolled back a small mapping change yesterday that altered how group names with prefix 'support-' are normalized. Can you confirm whether delegated_support hit normalization filter?

2026-03-13T18:02:01Z - Liam O'Connor: Confirmed. sso-proxy map_rules v2 strips hyphens and applies allowlist; it translated 'support-delegated' -> 'supportdelegated' which doesn't match RBAC role name 'delegated_support'.
2026-03-14T09:14:22Z - Aisha Patel: Several oncall engineers are still blocked; any ETA for workaround?

2026-03-14T10:01:05Z - Liam O'Connor: Workaround issued: admin can temporarily grant delegated_support via admin console for affected users. We're preparing a quick revert patch to mapping rules; target rollout to prod in next 2 hours behind feature-flag.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: mapping/normalization step in sso-proxy is over-normalizing Okta group names for ephemeral exchanges. Reproduced by creating an Okta session with group 'support-delegated' and confirming final token drops/renames role. Token-service currently trusts sso-proxy mapped claims and does not re-query SCIM groups. Checked token-service config (no recent changes). Reviewed deploy logs: sso-proxy v2026.03.12-mapping-v2 deployed to us-west at 2026-03-12T23:40Z. Mapping rules: strip non-alphanumeric, lowercase, apply alias table. The alias table lacks mapping for 'supportdelegated' -> 'delegated_support'. Also confirmed long-lived token flow (non-ephemeral) still preserves delegated_support, indicating bug specific to ephemeral mapping code path.
resolution: Workaround: Admins granted delegated_support to affected users via admin console (temporary). Short-term fix: rolled feature-flag to disable v2 normalization for ephemeral flow and deployed patch to sso-proxy (rollout started 2026-03-14T10:20Z to us-west, canary=10%). Long-term fix: update mapping alias table and add automated unit tests for group->role normalization; ticket created for config update and tests in auth-config repo. Post-deploy checks: instrumented token telemetry to assert expected roles present for ephemeral flows; will monitor for 24h. Follow-up: formal postmortem and add alert when role-count differs between Okta assertion and minted token.
